args: Analyze the bounds-safety root cause in pcpp::SSLClientHelloMessage::SSLClientHelloMessage in PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/SSLHandshake.cpp, especially extension parsing near reported line 1320. What length fields and helper types are involved, and what minimal robust bounds checks should be applied before reading an extension header, constructing specialized extension objects, and advancing? Mention any analogous safer parser in this source file.

The supplied ASan report shows a 2-byte heap-buffer-overflow while reading an extension type in SSLClientHelloMessage. The malformed ClientHello has a nonzero declared extensions block and an extension whose encoded payload length exceeds bytes remaining in the captured handshake and declared block. The current parser apparently creates an extension then advances curPos by getTotalLength() without validating that individual length. I need to patch only C/C++ under PcapPlusPlus and preserve parsing behavior for valid and truncated messages.
